title: Calloway as a disciplined leader and Buster Harding's farm system
summary: A band is no greater than its leader; Calloway demanded discipline and kept replacements ready through arranger Buster Harding.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, you see, Calloway himself -- you know, I've always said, and it's been said a lot of times, a band is no greater than its leader, --
-- you see. Calloway had a lot of class.
A lot of class, you know, and he believed in discipline. If you're going to do it, do it right. If you don't, get out, --
And he'd tell you in a minute. "Lay dead till Tuesday."
That's right. He'd tell you -- that's right -- "Lay dead and wait for Thursday." That was payday.
That was payday, Thursday. He was amazing.
But I'll never forget when a couple of guys was late or a couple of guys didn't act right, he looked at [ ] little boy in his place.
-- and Buster Harding used to be in New York? And Calloway would call up Buster and we used to say Buster was head of the farm system.
Yeah. "Pull out another guy right away."
